notes: Source of truth for all simulation parameters. Regenerate the Dart mirror with `dart run tools/gen_params.dart`. Every numeric entry is {value, source, note?}. Values marked 'initial estimate' must be verified in task T-103.

cellSizeM.source: Zensus 2022 100 m grid (Destatis, dl-de/by-2.0); 1 tile = 1 ha

tickMonths.source: design: one tick = one month. Recorded here as the convention the model is built on, not as a knob — nothing reads this entry. The month is hard-coded wherever it matters: seasons take the month as tick % 12, and the economy divides annual figures by 12. Changing this number would change nothing; changing the convention means changing those.

biotopeValue.source: BKompV Anlage 2: 34.07a.02 artenreiche frische (Mäh-)Weide = 18 (34.07a.01 Mähwiese = 20, 34.08a.01 Intensivgrünland = 8); modelled as extensive grassland developing from intensive to species-rich

recoveryMonths.source: Walker et al. 2004 (Biol. Conserv. 119, 1–18), via the Conservation Evidence summary: species-rich grassland sown on ex-arable land reached 50–81 % similarity to the target within 2–5 years, restoration by management alone gained slowly over 4–14 years; 10 years sits between the two. (An earlier citation of BfN-Schriften 721 for '10–15 years' is not supported by that text.)

co2PerHaYear.source: Poeplau & Don 2013 (Geoderma 192, 189–201): Umwandlung Acker → Grünland baut im Mittel 0,8 t C/ha/a Bodenkohlenstoff auf, also rund 2,9 t CO2/ha/a; Poeplau et al. 2017 (Sci. Rep. 7, 11550) mahnt für hochproduktive Ackerböden zur Vorsicht, deshalb der konservative Ansatz von 1 t CO2/ha/a. Das ist die Rate einer neu angelegten Wiese, nicht der deutsche Grünlanddurchschnitt: der ist laut UBA-Inventar 2024 mit 24,2 Mt CO2-Äq. auf 4,74 Mio. ha (Destatis 2025) eine Quelle von 5,1 t/ha/a, weil entwässerte Moorböden dominieren

airSink.source: design, anchored on Nowak et al. 2006 (i-Tree): Stadtbäume nehmen lokal einige Prozent des PM und NO2 auf. co2PerHaYear.source: Rate eines neu begründeten, wachsenden Bestandes, nicht des deutschen Waldes im Mittel. Waldgesamtrechnung (Thünen-Institut im Auftrag des Statistischen Bundesamtes): 52,5 Mt CO2 netto auf 10,7 Mio. ha Wald (2021) = 4,9 t/ha/a; die II. Altersklasse (21–40 Jahre) bindet am meisten, ein sich etablierender Mischwald rund 2,4 t C/ha/a = 8,8 t CO2/ha/a. Gegenprobe und Warnung: nach der Bundeswaldinventur 2022 ist der deutsche Wald 2017–2022 durch Kalamitäten zur Quelle geworden (UBA-Inventar 2024: Wald +2,1 Mt), der Spielwert gilt also für eine Aufforstung unter günstigen Bedingungen

areaReferenceDistanceM.source: half tile: boundary of a 1 ha area source; roads are split into 100 m segments (CNOSSOS-EU point-source segmentation)

areaDecayDbPerDecade.source: ISO 9613-2 / CNOSSOS-EU: geometric divergence of a point source, 6 dB per doubling; summing segments reproduces the 3 dB/doubling of a line

foliageAttenuationDbPerTile.source: ISO 9613-2 Table A.2 foliage attenuation up to ~10 dB over 200 m; simplified per 100 m tile

buildingScreeningDbPerTile.source: design, anchored on ISO 9613-2 und CNOSSOS-EU: eine geschlossene Bebauungszeile wirkt wie ein Schirm und bringt in der Praxis 5–10 dB Einfügungsdämmung; angesetzt ist der untere Rand, weil eine Spiel-Hektare keine geschlossene Zeile garantiert. ISO 9613-2 deckelt Einfachbeugung bei 20 dB

backgroundDb.source: TA Lärm Nr. 6.1: Immissionsrichtwert für reine Wohngebiete nachts 35 dB(A) — der niedrigste Wert der Tabelle und damit die ruhigste Umgebung, die die Verwaltungsvorschrift kennt. Das Feld fällt nirgends darunter

baselineThroughTraffic.source: design: any main road carries some through traffic

limitDayDb.source: TA Lärm: allgemeines Wohngebiet (WA) Tag 55 dB(A)

limitBadDb.source: TA Lärm: Gewerbegebiet 65; used as 0-score for residents

nightGuidelineDb.source: WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region (2018): road traffic Lnight below 45 dB (strong recommendation); Lden below 53 dB

nightLoaelDb.source: WHO Night Noise Guidelines for Europe (2009): Lnight,outside 40 dB is the guideline value and the lowest observed adverse effect level

nightHighRiskDb.source: WHO Night Noise Guidelines for Europe (2009): 55 dB is the interim target; above it cardiovascular effects become the major public health concern

decayLengthM.source: design, anchored on Pasquill-Gifford: das Modell ist ein Ersatz für eine Gaußfahne, keine Lösung einer solchen (docs/model/air.md). 300 m Abklinglänge heißt, dass eine Quelle nach 300 m auf 37 % und nach 600 m auf 14 % abgefallen ist — die Größenordnung, in der Straßenschluchten- und Nahfeldgradienten in der EMEP/EEA-Praxis abklingen. Auf einem 100-m-Raster ist das die Entscheidung, die zählt: drei Felder Abstand halbieren die Belastung mehr als einmal

sinkRadiusTiles.source: design, anchored on Nowak et al. 2006: die Deposition an Blattoberflächen wirkt lokal, im Bereich einiger hundert Meter. 3 Felder = 300 m auf diesem Raster

indexScale.source: calibration T-114: uniform housing_high + traffic (C≈0.4) → index ≈ 67; inside an industrial area (C≈3) → index ≈ 5

windFromDegrees.source: DWD: prevailing wind in Germany is from the south-west; meteorological convention, the direction the wind blows FROM. Only acts when windSpeedMs > 0.

windSpeedMs.source: design: calm by default so a scenario opts into wind through paramOverrides; DWD annual means for German lowlands are 3-4 m/s at 10 m

windStretchPerMs.source: Gaussian plume (Pasquill-Gifford): advection lengthens the plume downwind roughly in proportion to wind speed; 0.35 per m/s puts a 3 m/s wind at about twice the downwind reach

uhiMaxC.source: DWD, UHI-MAP – Urban Heat Island Rasterdatensatz für Deutschland, Version 7.0 (2024, CC BY 4.0), uhi_daymax_mean, 2022–24, maximum within 2 km of the centre of 12 towns of 6 000–23 000 residents: annual median about 0.8 K (0.2–1.8), summer about 1.1 K, hottest day about 2.4 K; cities of 75 000–770 000 reach 2.3–3.4 K. The model applies uhiMaxC as an annual-mean ceiling scaled by a monthly factor averaging 1, and a 1 ha hot spot runs hotter than a 1 km² mean, so 2 K for a small town. Cross-check: Dienst, Lindén & Esper 2018 (Clim. Res. 76, 1–15): Geisenheim, summer UHI 1.1 °C in nightly minima

greenPatchMinHa.source: InVEST Urban Cooling: green areas larger than 2 ha have an additional cooling effect

coolingDistanceTiles.source: InVEST Urban Cooling default d_cool = 450 m; game uses 3 tiles (300 m)

greenRadiusTiles.source: WHO Urban green spaces 2016: ≥0.5 ha within 300 m; 3-30-300 rule (Konijnendijk 2021)

retailM2PerResident.source: HDE Zahlenspiegel: ~1.4 m² Verkaufsfläche je Einwohner

retailReferenceSupply.source: calibration: one commercial tile at 300 m = full score (2000/3²)

jobDecayM.source: design: the local job-access indicator, jobs within cycling reach. Commutes decay far more slowly (commute.commuteDecayM, about 10 km), but on a 1.6–6.4 km map a 10 km kernel makes every cell's job access nearly equal, so the indicator would show nothing

jobReferenceJobs.source: calibration: ~one commercial + one industry tile within 500 m = full score, T-114

speciesAreaZ.source: Arrhenius / MacArthur–Wilson: z ≈ 0.25–0.35 for habitat islands

weight.source: design, anchored on InVEST Habitat Quality: das Handbuch sagt ausdrücklich, dass die Gewichte normiert werden und nur ihre Verhältnisse zueinander zählen — zwei Gewichtssätze unterscheiden sich nur, wenn sich die relativen Abstände unterscheiden. Die Spiel-Straße führt 10 000 Kfz/Tag und ist keine vierspurige Schnellstraße; 300 m liegt im unteren Bereich dieser Spannen

modeShareByDistance.source: MiD 2017 Ergebnisbericht (BMVI/infas) and MiD 2017 Analysen zum Rad- und Fußverkehr: walking dominates below 1 km but car already notable; cycling peaks at 1–1.5 km (21 %); car dominant from 1.5 km; commuting overall ≈ two thirds car, 21 % bike, 14 % walk

roadSearchRadiusTiles.source: design: 300 m to a main road counts as connected

commuteDecayM.source: Östh, Lyhagen & Reggiani 2016 (EJTIR 16(2), 344–363), Eq. 17: half-life method beta = ln 2 / median distance. Dauth & Haller, IAB-Kurzbericht 10/2018, pp. 1–4: median commute 10.5 km by road, about 30 % shorter straight-line, so about 7.4 km; 7.4 / 0.693 ≈ 10.6 km on the straight-line distances the map measures. A fit to IAB's distance classes gives about 14 km on road distances

externalCommuteKm.source: MiD 2017 Ergebnisbericht (BMVI/infas), pp. 62–63, Tables 8–9: mean work trip 16 km, 18–19 km in small-town and village areas, including trips that never leave the municipality, so those who leave travel further; BBSR (Pendeln 2023, press release 22.08.2024): mean one-way trip 17.2 km, a lower bound. 17–29 km is plausible

referenceCommuteKm.source: MiD 2017: mean one-way commute ≈ 16–17 km; a mean of 20 km scores zero on the distance half of the commuting indicator

transitWalkRadiusTiles.source: planning practice: the walking catchment of a tram or light-rail stop is usually taken as 400-600 m; 4 tiles is 400 m at this cell size

transitCarReduction.source: MiD 2017 Ergebnisbericht Abb. 18 / MiD 2023 Tab. 8: car 38 % vs 70 % and public transport 20 % vs 5 % between metropolis and rural village, so 15 pp ÷ 70 ≈ 0.21 of car trips (0.22 in 2023), a ceiling since the contrast also holds density and car ownership

cyclePathRadiusTiles.source: design: a cycle route is useful if it starts within a couple of hundred metres; 2 tiles is 200 m at this cell size

cycleCarReduction.source: MiD 2017 / MiD 2023: bike share 15 % vs 7 % (2023: 15 vs 6) between metropolis and rural village, 0.11-0.14 of car trips; RS1 feasibility study (RVR 2015): a cycle highway lifts cycling's share of non-walking trips from 10 % to 14-20 %
cycleCarReduction.note: design value, not a measured elasticity

cycleCompetitiveKm.source: MiD 2017 Analysen zum Rad- und Fussverkehr: cycling competes with the car on short trips and falls away beyond about 5 km, which is also where this model's own bins put the car above 85%

minCarShareFactor.source: MiD 2017 / 2023: car trips in the metropolis are 0.54 / 0.51 of those in a rural village; with access capped at 1 the transit and cycle reductions (0.2 + 0.15) never reach this floor, which only binds under scenario overrides

incomeTaxPerResidentYear.source: Destatis PM 126/2025: Gemeindeanteil Einkommensteuer 46.1 Mrd € (2024) ÷ 83.6 Mio EW ≈ 550 €

propertyTaxPerResidentYear.source: Destatis PM N006/2025: Grundsteuer B 15.1 Mrd € (2023) ÷ 84 Mio EW ≈ 180 €

businessTaxPerJobYear.source: Destatis PM 356/2024: Gewerbesteuer 75.1 Mrd € (2023) ÷ ~35 Mio SV-Beschäftigte ≈ 2 100 €

startBudgetKEur.source: design: enough for a 12-tile main road plus a mixed quarter of ~25 tiles

demolitionCostKEur.source: Sachsen, FRL Städtebauliche Erneuerung (15.02.2024), Nr. 5.2 c: demolition funded at up to 110 € per m² of demolished living space. Floor area per hectare is assumed, not sourced: about 1 400 m² in detached housing (11 homes × 130 m²) → 157 k€, about 4 700 m² in apartment blocks (67 × 70 m²) → 517 k€; 250 is one value across built tiles

immigrationRate.source: design, checked against German vacancy: with emigrationRate 0.008 the archetypes settle at 1.6-4.7 % vacant (Zensus 2022: 4.3 % nationally, 1.9-3.5 % in the largest cities, Stadt Köln KSN 13/2025), and fully attractive housing is 90 % full in 28 months: the pace of a new district, not of re-letting

emigrationRate.source: Techem, Umzugsquote 2014 (about 2 M flats; Wohnungswirtschaft heute 81, 2015, p. 25): 9.4 % of tenants move per year, 1−(1−0.094)^(1/12) = 0.0082 a month; Destatis Wanderungen 2025: 5.9 %/a leave their municipality, a lower bound. With immigrationRate 0.08 the archetypes settle at 1.6-4.7 % vacancy, against 4.3 % in Zensus 2022

unconnectedAttractivenessFactor.source: design, bracketed: no German study prices 'no main road within 300 m'; land whose access is not secured trades at 35-95 % of building land (Gutachterausschuss Northeim 2022, p. 3), and the Berlin areas that lost most rail access fell about 22 % (Ahlfeldt 2008, p. 22)

attractivenessWeights.source: design; relative importance from Wohnzufriedenheit surveys (BBSR) (initial estimate)

amplitude.source: design: 0 disables the yearly cycle entirely and reproduces the season-free model; a scenario can turn it down through paramOverrides

growth.source: DWD: the vegetation period in Germany runs roughly April to October, and evapotranspiration follows it. Monthly factors are scaled to average 1.0 over the year, so only the distribution within a year changes, not the annual total.

heat.source: DWD, UHI-MAP Version 7.0 (2024, CC BY 4.0), seasonal uhi_daymax_mean grids 2022-24 against the annual ones: for 12 towns of 6 000-23 000 residents (maximum within 2 km of the centre), the median season-to-annual ratio is winter 0.51, spring 0.98, summer 1.44, autumn 1.00. Fitted with an annual cosine peaking in July (amplitude 0.52, error 0.01 on the four seasonal means) and scaled to average 1.0. Until 2026-10-27 the factors ran 0.275-1.927, a summer 1.85 times the annual mean

zeroScoreTonsPerPerson.source: UBA, finale Daten 2024: 650 Mt CO2-Äq. in Deutschland, bezogen auf 83,5 Mio. Einwohner und 46,1 Mio. Erwerbstätige (Destatis 2024) = 5,0 t je Einwohner-oder-Arbeitsplatz. Eine Stadt, die emittiert wie Deutschland heute, bekommt damit 0 Punkte, eine klimaneutrale Stadt 100

designStormMm.source: KOSTRA-DWD-2020, grid field Spalte 118 Zeile 81 (INDEX_RC 081118), duration 60 min, return period 5 a: hN = 22.1 mm. A five-year hour is the ordinary heavy shower a drainage system is expected to cope with, not a disaster.

imperviousCurveNumber.source: USDA NRCS TR-55: connected impervious area, CN 98

initialAbstractionRatio.source: USDA NRCS TR-55: initial abstraction Ia = 0.2 S, the classical ratio

retentionRadiusTiles.source: design: open water and wetland take runoff from their immediate surroundings; 200 m at this cell size

retentionMmPerCell.source: HCU Hamburg et al., BlueGreenStreets Toolbox Teil B (2022), pp. 72-73: retention in open space with a storage depth of 50-200 mm; the geometric mean, 100 mm, is 1 000 m³ per water hectare

floodRiskMm.source: DWA-M 119 Tab. 1 (as reproduced in MULNV NRW, Arbeitshilfe Starkregenrisikomanagement 2018, Tab. 1): residential sewers overflow at most once in 2 years; KOSTRA-DWD-2020, cell 081118, 60 min, 2-year: 17.5 mm, through the model's runoff at CN 98: 12.5 mm
